approval: One hardware watchpoint observation, authorised by the user after the rule review.

tool.selftest_result: hit in 3.2 s with DR6 bit0 set

attempts.reason: my own scoping bug raised UnboundLocalError before the watch could arm; the client never started properly
watch armed on Engine.dll load and ran to the deadline

observed: With the watchpoint correctly armed on Engine.dll+0x421428 for the whole start-up and run, no write to those 8 bytes was trapped.
contradiction: An earlier session recorded the same slot as non-null at runtime (0x22ee236aeb0). That reading has NOT been reproduced in this session: the clean re-read attempt did not obtain an Engine.dll module at all (the client did not come up in that run), so it neither confirms nor refutes the old value.

possible_explanations.late_write: The write happens later than the observation window, for example when the graphics device or the level is created. Not tested.
possible_explanations.pre_arm_write: The write happened before the watch was armed, e.g. during loader notification ordering around Engine.dll DllMain. Not tested.
possible_explanations.stale_old_reading: The earlier non-null reading came from a process whose module base differed from the constant used at that moment. Not verified; the base was re-checked within that session and looked stable, but this cannot be proven now.

corrections_made.relocation_parser: My earlier relocation scan filtered type 3 (HIGHLOW). On PE32+ the relevant type is 10 (DIR64). Re-parsing with the correct type finds 7691 DIR64 entries, and still none inside 0x4213f0..0x421470, so the earlier conclusion survives, but the original filter was wrong.

honest_status: The watchpoint result is a negative result obtained with validated tooling. It does not identify the writer and it does not by itself invalidate the old reading; it shows that the write does not occur during the observed window.
not_claimed: that the slot is never written
that the old non-null reading was wrong
